title: Paul McCartney’s court hearing to dissolve The Beatles’ partnership – day five | 1971
content:
25 February 1971 was the fifth day of Paul McCartney’s court hearing to have The Beatles’ business partnership dissolved.

This was the second of two days in which a 46-page affidavit by Allen Klein, The Beatles’ business manager, was read out in London’s High Court. The statement was read by Morris Finer, QC, the barrister of John Lennon, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr.

Finer told the court that The Beatles had earned £7,864,126 between June 1962 and December 1968, and a further £9,142,533 in the 19 months between the beginning of Klein’s contract in May 1969 and December 1970. “Whatever else happens in this case,” said Finer, “they don’t want that interfered with.”
